name: substrate
owns: the machine underneath the interpreter: silicon behaviour, memory, the collector, the compiler, the kernel boundary
why_in_D: A web page runs on a CPU through a JIT with a heap and a kernel underneath it. Every one of those layers can be made to reveal or corrupt state without any application bug. Spectre was not a bug in a website. Rowhammer was not a bug in a website. They changed what a website could leak.

factors.name: speculative execution window
factors.def: the depth a core executes past a branch before resolution, which sets how much work is observable via cache state
factors.observable: cache timing differences between trained and untrained branch predictors

factors.name: branch predictor state
factors.def: the aliasing and training behaviour of the predictor, which lets one context poison another
factors.observable: cross-context timing asymmetry after training on a chosen address

factors.name: cache hierarchy sharing
factors.def: which cache levels are shared between siblings, cores and processes on the host
factors.observable: eviction-set mapping recoverable from access timing

factors.name: cache eviction policy
factors.def: whether the replacement policy is LRU, pseudo-LRU, or adaptive, which decides how clean a probe can be
factors.observable: measured reuse distance against predicted policy

factors.name: timing source resolution
factors.def: the granularity and coarsening of the clocks a page can read
factors.observable: variance of performance.now across calls under isolation settings

factors.name: timer coarsening policy
factors.def: the browser mitigation that quantises clocks to blunt side channels, and its residual signal
factors.observable: distribution of deltas around the quantisation step

factors.name: JIT tier thresholds
factors.def: the invocation counts at which code moves from interpreter to baseline to optimising compiler
factors.observable: discontinuity in per-call latency at a specific iteration count

factors.name: JIT optimisation assumptions
factors.def: the type and shape guards the optimiser inserts, and how they are invalidated
factors.observable: deopt storm when a type changes mid-loop

factors.name: JIT code page permissions
factors.def: whether generated code pages are simultaneously writable and executable, and for how long
factors.observable: memory map of a running engine

factors.name: WASM compilation pipeline
factors.def: how the engine compiles WebAssembly relative to JavaScript, including shared tiers and caches
factors.observable: tier-up timing of a wasm function against its JS twin

factors.name: WASM linear memory bounds
factors.def: the guard-page strategy that turns out-of-bounds access into a trap rather than a read
factors.observable: fault address on an out-of-bounds wasm load

factors.name: WASM memory growth semantics
factors.def: whether growing memory relocates the buffer, and what happens to views held across a growth
factors.observable: detached ArrayBuffer after a growth call

factors.name: allocator size classes
factors.def: the bucket sizes the heap allocator uses, which decides which allocations land in the same region
factors.observable: adjacency of objects of chosen sizes via pointer distance

factors.name: allocator reuse order
factors.def: whether freed chunks are reused LIFO, FIFO or by best fit, which decides heap grooming
factors.observable: address ordering of objects allocated after a free sequence

factors.name: allocator quarantine
factors.def: the delay before a freed chunk returns to general use, where engines keep one
factors.observable: reuse gap after free under allocation pressure

factors.name: heap layout determinism
factors.def: how much of the heap layout is reproducible across loads, which is the precondition for grooming
factors.observable: variance of object addresses across fresh sessions

factors.name: ASLR entropy budget
factors.def: the number of random bits behind the placements an attacker might need to guess
factors.observable: distribution of base addresses over many launches

factors.name: JIT region placement
factors.def: whether generated code is placed at a predictable offset from other regions
factors.observable: relative distance between code and heap mappings

factors.name: garbage collector algorithm
factors.def: the collector family in use, which decides pause shape and object movement
factors.observable: pause distribution under controlled allocation

factors.name: collector moving versus non-moving
factors.def: whether live objects change address, which decides whether a stale reference is a corruption primitive
factors.observable: address stability across a collection cycle

factors.name: finalizer and weak reference ordering
factors.def: when callbacks run relative to object death, which decides whether state is resurrected
factors.observable: ordering of finalizer output against a sentinel

factors.name: GC pause as a covert channel
factors.def: whether collection timing is observable enough to encode information across contexts
factors.observable: correlation between induced allocation and observed stall

factors.name: memory pressure signalling
factors.def: how the platform reports approaching limits, and whether a page can observe other pages' pressure
factors.observable: allocation failure timing shared across contexts

factors.name: per-context memory cap
factors.def: the ceiling on heap per tab or context, which is a denial-of-service boundary
factors.observable: point at which allocation throws rather than slows

factors.name: process versus thread isolation
factors.def: whether contexts share a process, and therefore an address space and an allocator
factors.observable: shared mappings in the process map

factors.name: site isolation granularity
factors.def: the unit at which renderers are split, which decides whether a leak crosses origins
factors.observable: distinct renderer pids per origin

factors.name: spectre-class gadget availability
factors.def: the presence of a code path that can be trained to speculatively read attacker-chosen memory
factors.observable: cache signal from a non-architectural read

factors.name: pointer authentication or tagging
factors.def: whether the architecture signs or tags pointers, and where the check is bypassed
factors.observable: behaviour of a forged pointer against the tag check

factors.name: memory tagging granularity
factors.def: the tag width and granule size, which decides whether a tag collision is brute forceable
factors.observable: probability of a valid tag by chance

factors.name: row hammer susceptibility
factors.def: the physical disturbance threshold of the memory, which is a corruption primitive with no software bug
factors.observable: bit flips under an access pattern, where testable

factors.name: kernel attack surface reachable from a renderer
factors.def: the syscalls and device interfaces a compromised renderer can reach
factors.observable: seccomp policy and reachable open descriptors

factors.name: sandbox broker interface
factors.def: the IPC surface through which a sandboxed process asks a privileged process to act
factors.observable: enumerable message types and their validators

factors.name: file descriptor inheritance
factors.def: which descriptors survive a spawn and are therefore reachable from a compromised child
factors.observable: descriptor table of a spawned helper

factors.name: shared memory segment exposure
factors.def: which shared mappings are readable by which process, which is a cross-boundary read primitive
factors.observable: map listing filtered by permissions

factors.name: huge page usage
factors.def: whether large pages are used, which changes both TLB behaviour and the granularity of a leak
factors.observable: mapping size and alignment

factors.name: swap and page cache exposure
factors.def: whether sensitive pages can reach disk or be inferred through cache state
factors.observable: page cache residency effects on timing

factors.name: CPU frequency and thermal state
factors.def: the dynamic frequency behaviour that changes timing baselines between runs
factors.observable: drift of a fixed workload's latency over minutes

factors.name: simultaneous multithreading sharing
factors.def: which execution resources two sibling threads share, which enables cross-thread leaks
factors.observable: contention signal from a sibling's workload

factors.name: instruction cache aliasing
factors.def: whether instruction fetch can be used as an oracle independent of data caches
factors.observable: timing difference on branch target after eviction

factors.name: prefetch behaviour
factors.def: whether hardware prefetching turns a near-miss into a signal, changing attack reliability
factors.observable: timing of adjacent versus distant addresses

factors.name: exception delivery semantics
factors.def: how faults are routed to the runtime, and whether a handler can be steered
factors.observable: which handler runs for a chosen fault class

factors.name: stack layout and canaries
factors.def: the arrangement of frames and the presence of a guard value, which decides exploitability of a write
factors.observable: frame layout under a controlled recursion

factors.name: control flow integrity coverage
factors.def: which indirect transfers are validated, and which are not, in the runtime itself
factors.observable: behaviour of an indirect call to a non-listed target

factors.name: entropy source health
factors.def: the quality and blocking behaviour of the random source, which decides whether tokens are guessable
factors.observable: statistical tests on generated values under load

factors.name: clock and counter monotonicity
factors.def: whether counters can go backwards or repeat, which breaks uniqueness assumptions
factors.observable: monotonicity violation under suspend or migration

factors.name: time zone and locale resolution
factors.def: the environment facts a page can read without permission, which feed fingerprinting
factors.observable: distinct value sets across environments

factors.name: suspend and resume effects
factors.def: what changes in clocks, connections and timers across a sleep, which is a state divergence
factors.observable: delta between expected and observed elapsed time

factors.name: emulation and virtualisation signals
factors.def: the artefacts that reveal a headless or virtualised environment, which decides whether a detection is fooled
factors.observable: comparison of collected signals against a baseline

factors.name: device and driver reachability
factors.def: which hardware interfaces are exposed to the browser process, each a kernel-adjacent surface
factors.observable: enumerable device nodes and permissions

factors.name: GPU driver command surface
factors.def: the command stream a page can submit through WebGL or WebGPU, which is privileged parsing
factors.observable: which commands can be issued and with what validation

factors.name: GPU memory residency
factors.def: whether GPU memory is cleared between contexts, which is a cross-context read primitive
factors.observable: content of a fresh buffer before write

factors.name: shader compiler behaviour
factors.def: the shader compiler as an attack surface and as a timing oracle
factors.observable: compile latency as a function of shader source

factors.name: audio and media codec parsers
factors.def: the native decoders a page can feed, each with its own memory-safety history
factors.observable: which formats are accepted and by which library

factors.name: font parsing surface
factors.def: the font rasteriser, historically one of the richest native parsers reachable from a page
factors.observable: which font tables are consumed and how

factors.name: interpreter for a second language in the page
factors.def: nested runtimes such as PDF JavaScript or SVG scripting, each with its own sandbox semantics
factors.observable: capability set available inside the nested context

factors.name: entropy of the process start state
factors.def: how much of the initial environment is attacker-influenced, which affects reproducibility
factors.observable: difference between two launches with the same inputs

factors.name: resource limit inheritance
factors.def: whether limits such as descriptors and memory are inherited by children, which is a denial boundary
factors.observable: limit values in a child process

factors.name: signal delivery from outside
factors.def: what an external process can force on a page's process, and how the page observes it
factors.observable: behaviour of the page after a forced signal

factors.name: core dump and crash artefact content
factors.def: what a crash writes to disk, which is a durable leak of page state
factors.observable: contents of a crash artefact after a controlled fault

factors.name: debug interface exposure
factors.def: whether a debugging or tracing interface is reachable and what it can read
factors.observable: whether attach succeeds and what it enumerates

factors.name: microcode and firmware revision
factors.def: the patch level that decides whether a mitigation is present or only advertised
factors.observable: revision reported by the CPU versus the mitigation list

factors.name: mitigation completeness
factors.def: whether a deployed mitigation covers every path or one documented path
factors.observable: a bypass found against the mitigated path
